scope: Image-service resource ownership and cancellation; synthetic fault injection, no CNN qualification or activation
fixes: Worker failures, including failure before the body starts, reach a terminal state and release image references.
Completed futures and exception tracebacks are not retained in job records.
File descriptor ownership is released when wrapping an opened image or JSON file fails.
POSIX tenant locks reject competing service instances and processes.
Spawned image jobs have deadlines that include queueing, selection, preflight, and execution.
Running cancellation and shutdown stop and reap owned processes without holding the asset-state lock while waiting.
Independent lifetime guards reclaim job, environment-probe, and inference groups after owner death.
Concurrent owner/watchdog termination retries after reaping; a permission denial is not treated as successful cleanup.
Interrupted service-owned output transaction siblings expire under retention, while active tokens remain protected.
A failed asset timestamp/stat operation does not leave a permanent active reference.
